s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance with a history of cardiac arrhythmia and pacemaker implantation
salient_findings: Gaze deviation in the right eye
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Presented to the emergency department
Has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation
Has a history of complete heart block
Has a pacemaker implanted in the late 1990s
Pacemaker was upgraded to a biventricular system
Blood pressure was 147/75 mm Hg
Heart rate was 84 beats per minute
Respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute
Oxygen saturation was 99% on room air
Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory
Electrocardiogram showed a ventricular-paced rhythm with ventricular bigeminy

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance, consistent with ischemic stroke symptoms

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of atrial fibrillation, which is a risk factor for cardioembolic stroke

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's atrial fibrillation history and presentation with stroke symptoms suggest a possible atrial fibrillation-related stroke

shortlist.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory, consistent with middle cerebral artery occlusion

shortlist.label: Thrombotic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of pacemaker implantation and atrial fibrillation may increase the risk of thrombotic stroke

raw.rationale: Patient has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation, which is a common cause of cardioembolic stroke, and the presentation of left-sided hemiparesis, dysarthria, and gaze deviation is consistent with a stroke in the middle cerebral artery territory.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as it does not specify the underlying cause of the stroke.

rejected.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
rejected.why: More of a specific location of the stroke rather than the type or cause of the stroke.

rejected.label: Thrombotic stroke
rejected.why: Less likely given the patient's history of atrial fibrillation, which suggests a cardioembolic source.

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
rejected.why: While this is a plausible diagnosis, cardioembolic stroke is a more specific and commonly used term to describe strokes caused by atrial fibrillation.
